methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series B → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.9x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Climate & Energy. Range: $700M - $3.0B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in Climate & Bio-Manufacturing

data.narrative:
Cemvita is a Series B climate and energy company founded by Moji and Tara Karimi that has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies—KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, and Amogy—supplemented by a broader universe of eight private peers and one public comparable (LNZA).

Two valuation methods were applied. Stage-progression methodology, using the $30M total raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, implies a valuation of $57M. Peer-median analysis across the three core comparables produced a median valuation of $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M (Amogy) to $3.0B (KoBold Metals). The peer-median method reflects both the sector's capital intensity and heterogeneity in maturity and technology focus within the narrow comp set.

Triangulation of these two methods yields a median implied valuation of $528M, with a low of $48M (conservative stage-progression floor) and a high of $1.1B (peer-weighted upside). The wide range reflects material uncertainty around technology differentiation, capital requirements to commercialization, and the limited liquidity events in frontier climate tech. Stage-progression yields a floor estimate; peer-median anchors to observable transaction precedent but underweights Cemvita's earlier stage relative to Series C comparables. Key variables affecting valuation include path to first commercial deployment and competitive positioning within hydrogen and synthetic biology subsectors.
